name: Strangers In Israel
overview: Scripture reveals that strangers in Israel were recognized as distinct yet integrated members of the community, sharing in certain religious privileges while observing specific laws. They were permitted to worship in the outer court of the temple and were subject to the same Sabbath rest as the Israelites, as seen in Exodus 20:10. However, restrictions applied, such as not eating the Passover unless circumcised (Exodus 12:43-44), and they were protected from oppression because the Israelites themselves had once been strangers in Egypt (Exodus 22:21). The law established one standard for both the native-born and the sojourning stranger, underscoring God's justice and mercy toward all residing within Israel (Exodus 12:49).
